questions.question: A motorcycle should fit you. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely touch the handlebars when sitting on the motorcycle.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to the motorcycle.
Your feet should reach the ground comfortably when sitting on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should reach the ground comfortably when sitting on the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can reach the ground comfortably while you sit on it. Always check that a motorcycle fits before you ride it.

questions.question: If vehicles or hazards are to your right, which side of the lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself in your lane to have the most space. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield is not a good replacement for a face shield.

questions.question: There is less braking traction when:

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle leans, such as in a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must do it carefully.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, it is important to:

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: It is most important to be aware of what is ahead of you. However, you must also know what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to track what is happening behind you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are stop signs. When you see one, you must come to a complete stop, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, keep a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle in front of you. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:

options.text: Goes into the bloodstream right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goes into the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It goes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and quickly reaches the brain.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as your motorcycle.
Take it out on the highway right away.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is at least somewhat different. Before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, learn where all the controls are. Practice in a safe, controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign appears on the back of slow-moving vehicles that travel below 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause a rider to:

options.text: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accidentally end up in another lane of traffic.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause a rider to cross into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before entering a turn or curve.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes since it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
Be comfortable, wearing shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other motorists can see you better.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing when riding to help other drivers see you better, even during the day.

questions.question: If riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
Clothing of any color because other drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Darkly-colored clothing to contrast with the bright sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brightly-colored clothing to increase your chances of being seen.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing to make yourself more visible while riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: The best way to avoid fatigue when riding your motorcycle on a long trip is to:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, limit your riding time each day and take frequent rest breaks. Do not use artificial stimulants because you may feel extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: When selecting a jacket for protection, a motorcycle rider should look for a jacket that is:

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a protective jacket when riding. Look for one that covers your arms completely, fits snugly but allows free movement. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: To minimize the potential for fatigue, you should:
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks during long trips to reduce fatigue. Caffeine and other stimulants can increase danger because you may become extremely tired when they wear off. Dress warmly for weather and consider a windshield for long rides to reduce fatigue.

questions.question: Before a ride, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. The throttle should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you release it, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of surviving a crash if you wear:
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards provides the most head and neck protection. Wearing a properly secured, quality helmet is the most effective thing you can do to survive a crash.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet and ankles best. They should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will soon turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Allow them to get in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow them to get in front of you.
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you at an even higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If vehicles are on both sides of your motorcycle, which lane position is usually safest?
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best. Good riders change their position based on road and traffic conditions. When vehicles are on both sides, the center lane position is usually the safest.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It has white background with red and black markings. This sign means right turns are not allowed.
